comments.author: greatergoodguy
comments.story: Microsoft Will Soon Bring Back The Start Menu In Windows 8.1
comments.text: This WAS predicted by many users and blogs prior to the release of Windows 8. Criticisms started a year prior to the official release of Windows 8, with the consumer preview version. Here's one of the videos. [VIDEO] This article was written shortly after the release but it does one of the best jobs of explaining how poor the usability of the OS is. [LINK]

comments.author: brownbat
comments.story: Windows 8 more widely used than OS X, IE still on the rise
comments.text: Yeah, I was shocked by the "dad" test: [VIDEO] And when Gabe talked about 8, I winced: [LINK] But watching a few "tips" / "best of new features" videos for 8.1... I start to feel a little left out. Just type to search. Re-engineered file copying. Hot corners make it seem like someone at least skimmed an article on Fitt's Law. And, ooh, Win + Print Screen? Just make the screenshot a file. Yeah, should have been fixed back in 95. So, er, maybe they got a few things right? I haven't upgraded yet, but... the dissonance is mounting.

comments.author: jser
comments.story: Windows 8 RTM 90-day free trial available to all, but seriously, don’t do it
comments.text: Tried using it in a virtual machine, but was an endlessly frustrating experience in Windows 8 (Metro) UI. It's like going from an iPhone to a Blackberry -- you want to touch the screen, but can't. Be prepared to be your family's help desk if they're buying a new machine: [VIDEO]

comments.author: webXL
comments.story: Windows 8 Release Preview ready for download
comments.text: They didn't need to take away the start button, and it's going frustrate a lot of users. See: [VIDEO] I've been running the preview in a VM, and getting back to the launcher frustrated me so much I had to install a small utility made by Stardock that makes a fake start button that takes you to the launcher: [LINK] . I'm a Mac guy, but my job requires me to be in Windows half the time. I hope they take a hint from Stardock and that video and put the start button back in.
